name: a bare host written in another script
why: A host is not spelled in Latin letters everywhere, and a renderer autolinks one that is not: it puts the host's punycode in the href, so the page carries a plain-http address off this site that is not even the string the reader saw. It needs no attacker -- a fact citing a Japanese or a Russian source, written the way it is written there, is this read. A fact writes a link as [text](url) and in no other form; a host in its prose goes in backticks.
fails: writes a link in a form this snapshot does not read

rows.source: Recorded 26 Oct 2026; figures at 日本.com/steal.
